result:
User-driven issue lifecycle events now carry the assignee's display name, so Hog templates can show who an issue is assigned to. I didn't run any tests, including the ones I extended.

**What changed**
- `products/error_tracking/backend/logic/lifecycle_events.py`: a new helper, `assignee_name_property`, looks up the display name from the assignee JSON.
  - For a user it is the full name, falling back to email. For a role it is the role name.
  - `prepare_issue_lifecycle_event` now adds `assignee_name` next to `assignee`, and `previous_assignee_name` next to `previous_assignee`.
  - Both keys are left out when the issue is unassigned, or when the user or role no longer exists.
  - The existing `assignee` JSON string is unchanged, so current exact-match filters keep working.
- `references/event-triggers.md` in the authoring skill has a new "Assignee properties" section. It documents the `assignee` JSON shape, when the key is absent, and the new name properties, so PostHog AI stops guessing.
- `test_error_tracking_api.py`: the existing assign and unassign lifecycle tests now also assert `assignee_name` and `previous_assignee_name`.

**Not covered**
Ingestion-driven events (`created`, `reopened`, `spiking`) come from the Rust cymbal notifications worker and don't get `assignee_name` yet. Adding it there needs a user and role name lookup in Rust, so I left it out. The skill doc says so.

Each lifecycle event now costs one extra user or role lookup. I skipped the alert-delivery Temporal payload path (`AlertDeliveryWorkflowInputs`), so the alert inputs still hold only the id.

 The three lifecycle events that error tracking alerts ride on. Each is fired by a different part of the
 ingestion / detection pipeline, has a different cadence, and exposes a different property surface.
 
+## Assignee properties
+
+Events that carry an assignee (`assigned`, and any user-driven transition on an assigned issue) expose:
+
+- `event.properties.assignee` is a JSON string, for example `{"type":"user","id":1234}` or `{"type":"role","id":"<uuid>"}`.
+  The key is absent when the issue is unassigned.
+  Hog templates cannot resolve the id, so use `assignee_name` for display.
+- `event.properties.assignee_name` is the assignee's full name (or email) for a user, or the role name for a role.
+  It is absent when the issue is unassigned.
+- `event.properties.previous_assignee` and `previous_assignee_name` describe the prior assignee on `unassigned` events.
+
+Ingestion-driven events (`created`, `reopened`, `spiking`) carry `assignee` but not `assignee_name`.
+
